findings.title: Descriptor scaler and abs boundary
findings.conclusion: H5 fits population mean/std on train descriptors only (279 global vectors; 4868 actual residues in saved scaler), uses scale=1 for constant columns, transforms actual residues then pads g with zero. h is abs(zscore(global)); g keeps signs. abs is applied once in H5 tensorize because it calls the encoder directly, not VAEModel.forward. Original wrapper also abs(global); H4 reconstruction runner uses the same declared train zscore. No latent parameter standardizer is in this path.
findings.limitation: abs is non-invertible and discards global descriptor sign relative to the mean, but is inherited/declared. The reconstruction pipeline does not need an inverse feature transform. Saved scaler metadata is checked without rereading train/dev/cohort records; historical preprocessing faithfulness is not claimed.

findings.title: DDPM target and latent axes
findings.conclusion: Encoder mu and logsigma are [B,16,48]; H5 stacks them at dim=1 as [B,2,16,48]. Channel0=mu, channel1=log standard deviation, positions=last axis including padded positions. findings.limitation: This excludes an identified axis or log-variance interpretation mismatch in inspected code; it does not prove DDPM has learned the target distribution. Padding positions are modelled, not masked out.

findings.title: No latent inverse standardization or inverse-flow omission
findings.conclusion: The DDPM cache stores native mu/logsigma without standardization, whitening, clipping or abs. Training adds diffusion noise in that coordinate system and generation consumes it directly. Therefore no missing latent inverse-scaler is identified. The posterior-parameter DDPM samples decoder-coordinate z=mu+sigma*epsilon and should go directly to decoder; inverse flow belongs to a different prior route.
findings.limitation: Standardizing these latent channels or clipping log scales would change the experiment and requires a new version; static consistency does not establish target adequacy.

findings.title: 999 coefficients versus 998 reverse updates
findings.conclusion: Both train and sample use a length999 linear beta[0..998] schedule (1e-4 to .02), alpha=1-beta, abar=cumprod(alpha). Training randint(1,999) gives t=1..998; generation reverses 998..1, conditional epsilon prediction, variance beta[t] and zero final noise at t=1. There is no t=999 access and no train/sample index range mismatch.
findings.limitation: The inherited schedule has abar[0]=.9999, not 1. The loop ends at index0 without an extra t0-to-clean transition. This is a precise endpoint convention/departure from an exactly clean endpoint, not evidence that it caused current latent mismatch. No correction or trajectory rerun was performed.

findings.conclusion: With use_prior_flow=True, training computes zp=prior_flow(z,g), evaluates Normal(0,1) density at zp, and decodes z. The original H4 empirical-condition-flow route explicitly selects a training descriptor and applies reverse flow.

findings.title: Epsilon not saved in CE recovery or MSE generated NPZ
findings.conclusion: Completed CE recovery/MSE generated arrays save posterior_parameters,z,raw,tokens,lengths,length_scores; posterior files save values only. The final randn_like(mu) is intended as a fresh standard-normal draw, but uses the same seeded generator stream after initial/reverse DDPM draws.
